answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents mint stake-backed identities anchored to cryptographic attestation chains, verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Genuine actors extract economic nectar from validated workflows, while identity creation incurs polynomial bonding staking costs that surge with network density. When a rogue swarm attempts mass replication, this fee schedule acts as an unyielding financial glacier, imposing exponential capital exhaustion where each duplicate identity generates a punishing cost ripple that rapidly drains attacker reserves.
